name: visual-b
thesis: Workbench elaborates the approved dark TNR console into calm, card-based surfaces where the only saturated colour on a screen is the authority lane you are standing in (cool blue to read, crimson to write, gold to publish), every risk state is a word plus a glyph plus a fill style, motion is spent only on transitions and progress, and an opt-in Daylight scheme keeps the same lane semantics for phone use outdoors. It keeps today's bones (scoped CSSOM tokens, createElement, 44px taps) and replaces the vocabulary that lets SENT, PAUSED and ORPHANED look like ordinary outline pills.

proposal.one_line: A calm, card-based operations bench on the approved deep-navy ground, where the only saturated colour on a screen is the authority lane you are standing in (cool blue to read, crimson to write, gold to publish), every risk state is a word plus a glyph plus a fill style, and motion is spent only on transitions and progress.

binding_elements_honoured: Deep navy/charcoal ground as the default theme: --bg #0c1017 / --paper #141a24 / --raised #1b2330 (amendment §3 'deep navy / charcoal / near-black surfaces', FORGE_NEXT_VISUAL_DIRECTION.md:40).

Crimson / gold / cool-blue accent family (amendment :43-45) mapped one-to-one onto the three authority lanes: cool blue = READ and ordinary chrome, crimson = LIVE WRITE, gold = PUBLISH and Content Admin identity. Semantic green/amber/red stay reserved for VERIFIED / caution / FAILED (amendment :46-48).
Layered depth: two elevation steps (--paper cards on --bg, --raised for the top bar, bottom bar, inspector, toasts) with --shadow-raised; no flat grey boxes (amendment :41).

Hard-edged ink-inspired controls used selectively (amendment :52-56): only the three buttons that touch the game (Send writes, Publish, Reconcile & resume) are square with a 4px offset ink shadow; everything else keeps a 10-12px radius, so the shape itself says 'this one touches production'.
Operation-mode band (READ ONLY / LIVE WRITE / PUBLISH / RECOVERY) with counts above every actionable card (amendment §8, :148-171).

State rules of amendment §9 (:173-188): active work has a separate progress element; verified work is decisively finished; paused/incomplete/recovery are distinct from success and failure; SENT never looks retry-safe; auth unavailable, refused and read failure are three states; read-only looks safer than live-write; full capture persistence stays visible; publishing has its own treatment; nothing is colour-only.

Controlled motion of amendment §10 (:190-208): card/selection transitions, active-lane edge response, progress animation, smooth expansion; no ambient motion in data views, nothing behind confirmations, nothing cinematic.

Strong Forge identity: a typographic FORGE wordmark (system font, 800 weight, tracked) with a crimson rule, in the rail and phone top bar; no fetched logo asset (amendment §12 lists the exact logo as illustrative).

departures_for_director_decision.departure: Opt-in light 'Daylight' scheme beside the dark default
departures_for_director_decision.why: the operator works on a Samsung phone in Firefox (docs/00_INDEX.md:3-4) and a dark UI under sun glare loses perceived contrast; a light scheme with the same lane semantics keeps the tool usable outdoors. Evidence tier: Inferred (no measured daylight session in the repository). The default stays dark, so the approved character is what ships unless the operator switches.
departures_for_director_decision.cost: every token pair is checked twice (205 pairs, all pass); ~1.6 KB more CSS; a Settings toggle
departures_for_director_decision.recommendation: ship it opt-in with dark default; drop it if the director prefers a single dark look

departures_for_director_decision.departure: Content-lane cards carry a muted decorative edge and a glyph, not vivid per-lane imagery
departures_for_director_decision.why: Workbench reserves saturated colour for authority; the mockup's vivid lane art (crimson Combat, blue Items, gold Quests, violet Characters) reuses the exact hues the lanes and SENT need to own. Muted teal/steel/sand/moss edges (all ≥3:1 vs paper, table rows 'decor edge …') keep lanes recognisable without spending the authority hues. Also: a userscript bundle cannot fetch imagery; any lane art would be data-URI bytes on a 397,984-byte bundle (docs/forge_next/A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:171-177).
departures_for_director_decision.cost: less 'atmospheric' Command Center than the mockup
departures_for_director_decision.recommendation: muted edges in v1; revisit with a byte budget if the director wants art

departures_for_director_decision.departure: No hero illustration; texture is CSS-generated
departures_for_director_decision.why: no external assets at runtime; a data-URI hero costs bundle bytes parsed on every game page the loader matches (A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:177). Workbench uses a static two-stop navy gradient plus a repeating-linear-gradient hairline texture in the Command Center hero and empty states only (amendment :57 allows texture in non-critical areas).
departures_for_director_decision.recommendation: CSS texture in v1; a ≤20 KB data-URI illustration is a later, separately budgeted decision

departures_for_director_decision.departure: The approved family's two hue collisions are resolved by role, not by changing the family
departures_for_director_decision.why: crimson (action) sits 15-20° from danger red, and gold sits near caution amber (informational rows 'HUE ADJACENCY …', 1.94:1 and 1.23:1 in dark). Workbench never uses crimson as text on a surface in dark (3.64:1 would fail AA) and never uses danger red as a fill; gold is fill/text for publish and admin identity, amber is text/tint for caution and is never a band. Every state still carries a word and a glyph.
departures_for_director_decision.cost: a code-review rule (mut never a pill, warn never a band) rather than a palette guarantee
departures_for_director_decision.recommendation: accept the role rule; if the director wants a palette guarantee, shift danger to orange-red #ff8f73 (dark) / #b3350f (light) or shift caution to a paler straw

design_tokens.mechanism: All custom properties live on `.f-host, .f-app, .f-boot` (never :root) exactly as today (forge/src/ui/styles.mjs:11,19-20,59), so the carrier page under the overlay is never restyled (forge/src/ui/takeover.mjs:41-43,54). Dark values are the base block. The light block is `.f-host[data-theme="light"], .f-app[data-theme="light"], .f-boot[data-theme="light"] {…}` and, only if the director enables 'follow system', an additional `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { .f-host:not([data-theme="dark"]) … }` block. installCss() keeps @media blocks intact because splitRules() only splits at brace depth 0 (forge/src/ui/dom.mjs:44-52). `color-scheme` is set per block so native inputs, scrollbars and the file picker match.

lane_semantics.acc_and_read: One cool chakra blue for both, on purpose: reading is the app's default posture, so ordinary chrome (nav current, focus ring, links, the Run captures button) and the READ lane share it. A screen with only blue on it is, by construction, a screen that cannot write.
lane_semantics.mut: Crimson, used ONLY on surfaces that can send a mutation: the LIVE WRITE band (solid crimson, white text, 4.8:1 dark / 7.82:1 light), the square Send button, the 3px top-bar underline while a mutation job is RUNNING, and the 6px left rail of a mutation card. In dark it is never text on a surface (3.64:1, recorded as informational); it is a fill that text sits on.
lane_semantics.pub: Gold, used ONLY for player-visibility and Content Admin identity: the PUBLISH band (gold fill, ink text, 11.24:1 dark / 8.3:1 light), the square Publish button, the PUBLISHED pill, the Admin rail glyph. In light the fill #d9ad2e is decoration inside a 2px #6f5400 border (3.39:1 vs the fill) and the words carry the identification, because gold on white is 2.11:1 (recorded as a known, mitigated gap).
lane_semantics.warn: Amber for PAUSED, INCOMPLETE, advisories and the orphan card's dashed border and cap; text/tint only, never a band, never a button fill.
lane_semantics.sent: Violet, reserved for exactly one meaning: a request left the device and has no decoded answer. Nothing else in the app is violet; the Reconcile & resume button is the only violet fill and it appears only when a SENT item exists.
lane_semantics.ok_bad: Green and red are verdict colours (VERIFIED / FAILED, verdict banners, the SIGNED OUT chip). Red is never a fill except the SIGNED OUT chip; a red fill would collide with the crimson band.
lane_semantics.decor: Teal, steel, sand and moss are decorative content-lane edges on the Command Center only; they are not permitted on any job, item, pill, band or verdict.

design_tokens.pill_anatomy: h("span", { class: "f-pill SENT", "aria-label": "state SENT: request left this device, no server answer" }, h("i", { class: "f-g", "aria-hidden": "true" }, "◐"), "SENT"). Glyph box 16x16 with fixed width so a missing glyph (tofu) cannot shift the label; 12px/700 label with .04em tracking, min-height 24px; 1px border in the fg colour for outline/tint styles; hatched style adds `background-image: repeating-linear-gradient(135deg, var(--hatch) 0 4px, transparent 4px 8px)` over --t-sent; inverted-solid (ORPHANED) is --orph-fg on --orph-bg with no border, the only pill that flips the page polarity; solid-gold (PUBLISHED) is --on-pub on --pub-fill with a 1px --pub border in light. Existing class names (.f-pill.FAILED etc.) are kept so forge/test/ui.test.mjs:116 still selects them.

known_gaps_mitigated: light: KNOWN GAP gold fill (pubFill) vs white paper: below 3:1, so the light PUBLISH band and Publish button carry a 2px dark-gold (pub) border and the words; the fill is decoration, the border+words identify the control = 2.11:1

lowest_text_pair.pair: pill VERIFIED fg on its bg

contrast_summary.method: WCAG 2.x relative luminance (sRGB linearised with the 0.04045 threshold, 0.2126/0.7152/0.0722 weights) and (L1+0.05)/(L2+0.05); computed by scratchpad/design/contrast.mjs through palette_b2.mjs, not estimated. Thresholds: 4.5:1 for every text pair (pill text is 12px/700, which WCAG does not count as large, so it is held to 4.5), 3:1 for rails, rings, fills, meters and segments (1.4.11).

typography.family: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif; mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", Menlo, Consolas, "Roboto Mono", monospace. No @font-face, no fetch: the bundle is one @require file (forge_loader_user.js:12) and must stay self-contained. On Samsung Android Firefox system-ui resolves to Roboto (or Samsung One if the user chose it), which is the face the operator already reads the game in. The FORGE wordmark is the same family at 800 weight with .12em tracking and a 2px crimson rule under it; no display face is bundled (amendment :212 allows a display face 'sparingly', Workbench declines the bytes).

scale_phone_390.counts: font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums everywhere a number can change

why_it_reads_at_390_in_daylight: Base 16px instead of today's 15px (styles.mjs:19) and line-height 1.5: on a 390px Samsung panel at ~2.75x that is ~44 device pixels per line, above the size at which Roboto's x-height stops mattering outdoors.

Dark default pairs are all ≥7:1 for body and meta (ink 15:1 on paper, mute 7.78:1; contrast_table), which leaves headroom when glare halves perceived contrast; the opt-in Daylight scheme is 17.49:1 / 7.54:1 for the same pairs.
No weight below 400 and no hairline colour text: every coloured word is ≥4.65:1 on the surface it sits on, and every state word is also bold (700).
13px floor for meta and mono; the only 12px text is the pill label and the h3 label, both 700 and uppercase-tracked.
Line length is capped at ~60ch in the centre column (max-width 720px) so desktop does not become a wall; on the phone the column is the viewport minus 12px gutters.

spacing_and_density.touch_target_min: 44 x 44 CSS px for every button, row, nav item and pill-with-action (today: buttons 44, nav 40, styles.mjs:27,31); the three ink buttons are 48 tall on phone; list rows min-height 56 so a row is one comfortable thumb target; bottom nav items 56 tall, 64 with the label.

card_widths.390x844: one column; card = 366px (390 - 2x12); content-lane cards on the Command Center are 2-up, 177px each with a 12px gap
card_widths.768x1024: one centred column, card = 720px; Command Center tiles 2-up at 352px with a 16px gap; the bottom nav stays until 1024
card_widths.1280x800: three regions: nav rail 200px | centre 720px | inspector 296px, 16px gaps and 16px outer gutters = 1280 exactly; above 1280 the centre grows first to 800px, the inspector stays 296px

spacing_and_density.bottom_action_bar: Phone/tablet only: a sticky bar 64px + env(safe-area-inset-bottom) on --raised with --shadow-raised that holds the screen's primary action (lane-coloured, square if it touches the game) and one secondary. It sits ABOVE the bottom navigation (56-64px), so a Run screen on a phone reserves 120-128px at the bottom; when a screen has no primary action the bar is not rendered. On desktop the actions move into the header row and neither bar exists.
spacing_and_density.bottom_nav: Phone/tablet: five items maximum (Home, Manifests, Run/Active, Recovery, More), each a 24px glyph over a 12px label, current item in --t-acc with a 3px --acc top edge; the Recovery item carries a solid violet dot when any SENT item exists anywhere in the journal (journal.resumable(), forge/src/storage/journal.mjs:358-366) and a solid amber dot for a PAUSED job; dots are static.

operation_mode_band.rule: One band caps every preflight, run, publish and recovery card; the words and the glyph come first, the counts come from the planned items (plan.filter(op==='create').length, updates, captures.length, persist:'full' count; screens.mjs:116-121,153-154 already compute them) and never from a live poll. The four bands differ in fill lightness (solid / tint / gold / tint), rail width, glyph and words, so a protanope sees four different caps.

job_progress.rule: One segment per item in plan order, drawn as child elements (h("i", { class: "f-seg VERIFIED", "aria-label": "item 3 VERIFIED" })), never a gradient, so the DOM is the legend. Fill styles are redundant with colour: solid = server answered (CONFIRMED/VERIFIED), hatched = SENT, hollow = PLANNED, dashed outline = SKIPPED, solid red with ✕ = FAILED, inverted with ? = ORPHANED. Above 40 items the segments collapse into a grouped proportional bar with the same fills and the count line becomes the legend; the largest write manifest in repository history is 31 entries (harvests/inbox/tnr_results_1788135094828.json) and 26 items (archive/spent-manifests/push-2026-09-09/29_hide_not_ours.json), so the per-item form covers everything committed. The count line is aria-live="polite". Today's bar (styles.mjs:50-51, screens.mjs:171) is one accent fill of done/total that turns amber on pause; it cannot show that one item is SENT.

publish_state.rule: Content lifecycle pills share the job-pill anatomy. HIDDEN is a dotted hollow circle in --mute (the safe default reads as quiet, docs/00_INDEX.md:100-101), PUBLISHED is a solid gold pill with a fisheye glyph so 'visible to players' is the loudest of the three. A publish in flight shows a hatched violet 'PUBLISH SENT' pill until read-back, then flips to PUBLISHED only on VERIFIED; the pill never flips on HTTP success (docs/forge_next/A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:145).

status_visualization.command_center_system_status: The System Status block is four static chips fed without a live poll: auth (AuthState), repository listing (app.state.pickerAt / pickerError), storage persisted (app.state.persisted, app.mjs:408-410), budget (Budget.status() tripped/used). Each chip is glyph + word + detail; a chip that cannot be known says 'not checked' in --mute, never green.

risk_states.today: Risk states today are outline pills of equal weight (styles.mjs:42-45: SENT violet outline and CONFIRMED blue outline look alike; ORPHANED, PAUSED and INCOMPLETE share one amber outline), four banner kinds (styles.mjs:48-49: .f-banner.warn/.bad/.ok/.info), a single-colour progress bar (styles.mjs:50-51), disabled buttons at opacity .45 (styles.mjs:32) and a mutation-ness expressed only in the window.confirm text (screens.mjs:151-156, app.mjs:172-175) and the absence of the read-only info banner (screens.mjs:122). The Run screen of a mutation job and of a capture job look identical while running (screens.mjs:169-172,220). A paused job on Jobs is a .f-banner.warn (screens.mjs:18-26) whether it paused for a clock or for an unresolved SENT.
risk_states.mutation_screen: Every preflight and run card of a job with items gets the LIVE WRITE band: a 44px solid crimson cap with white text (4.8:1 dark, 7.82:1 light), a 6px crimson rail down the card, the ◆ glyph and '3 creates · 1 update'; the primary button is the square crimson ink button reading 'Send 4 writes to the game', not 'Start job'; while a mutation job is RUNNING the sticky top bar carries a 3px crimson underline on every screen (3.29:1 vs --raised), so navigating away does not hide that a write may be in flight. Read-only jobs get the READ band in --t-acc with ◇ and 'READ ONLY · zero mutations' and a rounded blue button 'Run captures'. The two differ by fill lightness, glyph, words, rail width and button shape.
risk_states.publish_action: Publish is its own lane (gold) and never shares a button style with Send. The square gold ink button opens an inline two-step strip inside the same card: 'This makes Ember Palm visible to every player. [Cancel] [Publish]', Confirm disabled for 600ms and placed at the far end of the strip from the trigger. No window.confirm: the native dialog is unstyled, cannot carry the lane or the counts, and looks the same for a cache clear and a live write. The strip is static (120ms slide only, none under reduced motion). Publishing is a full update that flips hidden (or published on guides) and must read back (docs/forge_next/K_USER_DECISIONS.md:79); Forge has no publish action at all today (docs/forge_next/A_ARCHITECTURE_MAP.md:151), so this is a new surface, not a restyle; the UI shows PUBLISH SENT until the read-back.

The row gets a violet rail and a caption 'Request left this device; the server has not answered. Forge reconciles, never resends.' The job header gains a solid violet chip '1 unresolved write' that cannot be dismissed. On Home and Recovery, an open job with any SENT item is a full card (not a banner) capped with the RECOVERY band 'UNRESOLVED WRITE · reconcile before anything else'; its only primary action is the square violet ink button 'Reconcile & resume' (the label already exists, screens.mjs:24); no Send verb is visible anywhere on that card. proposal.what_it_borrows_from_the_game: Two things, both selectively and both named in the amendment (:52-56). (1) The square ink button with an offset shadow: the current client's `.tnr-ink-btn-primary` is `border-radius: 0; border: 2px solid #26110c; box-shadow: 5px 5px 0 #b7331f` and its hover translates 2px with the shadow shrinking to 3px (app/src/styles/globals.css:243-289 in the scratchpad clone of studie-tech/TheNinjaRPG at head 36c5873b; this class does not exist at the Forge pin 345d18ac, whose button.tsx uses rounded-md and shadow-xs, app/src/components/ui/button.tsx:16-27). Workbench uses that silhouette for exactly the three buttons that touch the game, with its own tokens (--shadow-ink in --ink/--bg, 4px) so the game's parchment fill and brick-red shadow are not copied. (2) The dark navy rather than pure black: the game's `.dark` layout is `--background: 222 47% 11%` (globals.css:137-141 at the pin); Workbench's --bg #0c1017 is in the same family and reads as 'the game's world at night' without copying its values. Rejected from the game: the parchment ground (`--background: 55 92% 95%`, globals.css:103) because a warm surface would blur the overlay boundary, and the bundled Open Sans (app/fonts/OpenSans.ttf) because the bundle must not fetch. Forge is an overlay above the game and should look like the tool, not the world.
rejected_alternatives: Workbench revision 1 (this panel's earlier draft): light-by-default with blue/orange/plum lanes. Rejected because the director settled the character mid-pass (dark, crimson/gold/blue); its contrast tables and density rules survive here, its palette and default do not.
Dark-only continuation of today's tokens (styles.mjs:11): keeps the outline-only pills and the opacity-disabled buttons that make risk states quiet now, and offers nothing for daylight use.
Parchment / game-matched theme: the overlay would read as part of the game, and warm paper eats the crimson lane.

Hue per content type on job surfaces (jutsu green, item blue, quest gold…): the hue budget is spent on authority and state; content type is a label and a glyph, never a colour, except the muted decorative edges on the Command Center.
Vivid per-lane imagery as in the mockup: reuses the authority hues and costs data-URI bytes on every game page; recorded as a director decision, not silently dropped.
Glass / translucent surfaces over the carrier: backdrop-filter is expensive on Android Firefox, and a translucent overlay would let the game page show through behind a verdict.
Pulsing or breathing SENT pill: the most tempting way to say 'unresolved', and exactly what the non-negotiables forbid; the hatch, glyph and caption say it without motion.
Square ink buttons everywhere: the shape would stop meaning anything; reserving it for the three game-touching buttons is what makes it a signal.
A single accent plus red (monochrome bench): calm, but it cannot make read and write look different, which brief §6 requires (state/prompt_forge_next_planning.md:218).

Inline SVG icons via createElementNS: legal under the DOM law and crisper than Unicode, but ≈2 KB of path data and more code for v1; recorded as the upgrade path if Samsung Firefox renders any geometric glyph as tofu.
Keeping window.confirm for Publish and Send: the native dialog is unstyled, cannot show the lane or the counts, and looks the same for a cache clear and a live write.
Bundling a display face for the FORGE wordmark: forbidden by the self-contained bundle rule unless embedded as a data URI, which costs 20-60 KB for one word.

weaknesses: The approved family puts crimson beside danger red and gold beside caution amber (dark: 1.94:1 and 1.23:1 apart); Workbench separates them by role (crimson only as fill, red only as text; gold as fill/identity, amber as text/tint) and by glyph, which is a code-review rule rather than a palette guarantee.

Crimson cannot be text on a dark surface (3.64:1), so every mutation word must sit on the crimson fill; a future screen that wants a crimson caption on --paper will fail AA and must use the band instead.

The light Daylight scheme's gold fill is 2.11:1 on white; it relies on its dark-gold border and words. If the director wants a pure-colour guarantee in light, the publish fill must darken to ≈#b8901c and lose some of the 'gold' look.
Unicode glyph rendering on Samsung Firefox is Inferred, not verified; if ◐ or ◔ is tofu the redundancy drops to word + fill style (still two channels). Inline SVG is the fallback and costs code.
Two themes double the contrast surface; the proposed token test mitigates, but every future colour tweak has to pass both blocks.
The 1.5s whole-main re-render while running (app.mjs:268,87) defeats progress transitions unless the progress element is patched in place; that is a small but real change to RunScreen's render model.

Replacing window.confirm with an inline strip for Send/Publish changes a tested flow (ui.test.mjs:149,178,216) and adds ~50 lines of confirm logic that itself needs adversarial tests (double-tap, arming delay under reduced motion).

Two sticky bottom bars on a phone Run screen (action bar + nav) cost 120-128px of an 844px viewport; the fold arithmetic still fits the lane, state, problem and three items, but a job with a long pause detail will scroll.
The desktop inspector introduces a second place that renders budget/auth; it must read the same objects as the centre column or the two can disagree.

The muted content-lane treatment is calmer than the approved mockup's vivid lanes; if the director wants the mockup's atmosphere back, Workbench needs a byte budget for data-URI art and a rule keeping that art off every stateful surface.
user_decisions_surfaced: Ship the opt-in light Daylight scheme (dark stays default) or a single dark look (K-01 residue; recommendation: ship opt-in).
If Daylight ships: 'auto / follow system' allowed, or explicit dark|light only (recommendation: explicit only, to avoid a light overlay flashing over the game's dark pixel layout).
Content-lane cards: muted decorative edges + glyph (Workbench) vs vivid per-lane imagery as in the mockup (needs a data-URI byte budget and a rule keeping art off stateful surfaces).
Hero treatment: CSS gradient + hairline texture (Workbench) vs a ≤20 KB data-URI illustration.
Hue-collision policy: accept role separation (crimson fill / red text; gold fill / amber text) or shift danger to orange-red (#ff8f73 dark / #b3350f light) for a palette-level guarantee.
Square ink buttons reserved for the three game-touching actions (Send / Publish / Reconcile) as proposed, or a wider use that weakens the signal.
Confirmation model for Send and Publish: inline two-step strip with a 600ms arming delay (proposed) versus keeping window.confirm.
Glyph technology: Unicode geometric shapes (proposed, zero bytes) versus inline SVG via createElementNS (crisper, ~2 KB, more code).
State words stay uppercase journal vocabulary (SENT, ORPHANED) as proposed, or become sentence case.
Top-bar crimson underline while a write job is RUNNING: on every screen (proposed) or only on Run.
Whether two sticky bottom bars on the phone Run screen are acceptable, or the primary action stays in the header as today.
